title: MQTT packet (fixed header)
summary: MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) packets: fixed header (1 byte: packet type 4 bits + flags 4 bits, then variable-length remaining length), then variable header (packet ID, topic name, etc.), then payload. Packet types: 1 CONNECT, 2 CONNACK, 3 PUBLISH, 4 PUBACK, 5 PUBREC, 6 PUBREL, 7 PUBCOMP, 8 SUBSCRIBE, 9 SUBACK, 10 UNSUBSCRIBE, 11 UNSUBACK, 12 PINGREQ, 13 PINGRESP, 14 DISCONNECT, 15 AUTH.

structure.meaning: 1 CONNECT, 2 CONNACK, 3 PUBLISH, 4 PUBACK, 5 PUBREC, 6 PUBREL, 7 PUBCOMP, 8 SUBSCRIBE, 9 SUBACK, 10 UNSUBSCRIBE, 11 UNSUBACK, 12 PINGREQ, 13 PINGRESP, 14 DISCONNECT, 15 AUTH.
PUBLISH: DUP (bit 3), QoS (bits 1-2), RETAIN (bit 0). Others: reserved (must be 0) except PUBREL/SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE (must be 2).
Number of bytes remaining in the packet (max 268,435,455). Each byte: 7 bits of data + 1 continuation bit.
CONNECT: protocol name, version, flags, keep alive, properties. PUBLISH: topic name, packet ID (if QoS > 0), properties.
CONNECT: client ID, will topic, will payload, username, password. PUBLISH: application message. SUBSCRIBE: topic filters + QoS.

ext.example_decoded: MQTT CONNECT packet: type 1, remaining length 16, protocol 'MQTT', version 5, clean start, keep alive 60
notes: MQTT 5.0 adds properties, reason codes, shared subscriptions, and topic aliases.
QoS levels: 0 (at most once), 1 (at least once), 2 (exactly once).
Retained messages are stored by the broker and delivered to new subscribers.
MQTT is the standard for IoT messaging (sensors, actuators, telemetry).
